notes: Gold = production Ruby code (app/, lib/, config/, plugins/*/lib), specs excluded. Most tasks target features added in 2026 that models cannot answer from memory: the built-in MCP server and its OAuth flow (lib/discourse_mcp), passwordless email login codes, the nested-replies hot sort and upcoming-change promotion. Several symbols are only reachable through Rails/Service::Base metaprogramming (`rate_limit` after_create blocks, `model :x` -> `fetch_x`, `policy :name` steps). Ruby bang/predicate names (`consume!`, `should_autosilence?`) are written with their suffix. `search` is the phrase an agent would derive from the question (English, no identifier the developer did not give). Re-check with `kopt bench discourse --verify`.

tasks.question: When an MCP client exchanges an OAuth authorization code for tokens on Discourse's built-in MCP server, where is the PKCE code_verifier checked against the stored code challenge?
tasks.search: mcp oauth authorization code exchange pkce code verifier challenge
tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/discourse_mcp/oauth.rb@v2026.9.0: DiscourseMcp::OAuth::TokenIssuer.exchange_code! (264) looks the code up by digest, locks it, rejects consumed/expired codes, client_id, redirect_uri and resource mismatches, then calls secure_compare_challenge (391: verifier must match PKCE_VERIFIER_PATTERN, S256 = urlsafe base64 of SHA256(verifier) compared with secure_compare) before marking the code consumed and issuing access and refresh tokens.

tasks.question: In the nested (threaded) replies view, where is the 'hot' score of a reply computed from its likes, its direct replies and a freshness bonus that decays with a half-life?
tasks.search: nested replies hot score likes replies freshness bonus half life
tasks.verifiedBy: Read lib/nested_replies/hot_score_calculator.rb@v2026.9.0: NestedReplies::HotScoreCalculator.score_for (64, Ruby) and hot_score_sql (41, the same formula as a SQL CASE expression) compute ln(1 + max(like_score*like_weight + direct_replies*reply_weight, 0)) + freshness_max_bonus * 0.5^(age / half_life) for public posts, HOT_SCORE_FLOOR otherwise; the weights come from formula_settings (13, nested_replies_hot_* site settings).

tasks.question: Where does Discourse decide to automatically silence a new user whose posts were flagged as spam by several different users, and how is the spam score threshold computed?
tasks.search: automatically silence new user spam flags score threshold
tasks.verifiedBy: Read @v2026.9.0: SpamRule::AutoSilence#should_autosilence? (auto_silence.rb:19) skips staged users and TL1+, then requires num_users_to_silence_new_user > 0, total_spam_score >= Reviewable.spam_score_to_silence_new_user and spam_user_count >= num_users_to_silence_new_user; user_spam_stats (29) sums pending/agreed spam reviewable scores and counts distinct flaggers in SQL; Reviewable.spam_score_to_silence_new_user (reviewable.rb:317) = sensitivity_score(silence_new_user_sensitivity, scale: 0.6). perform calls silence_user -> UserSilencer.auto_silence.

tasks.question: With passwordless sign-in by emailed code, where is a submitted 6-digit login code checked, and how are wrong guesses counted so the code cannot be brute-forced?
tasks.search: email login code verify submitted code attempts brute force hash
tasks.verifiedBy: Read app/models/email_login_code.rb@v2026.9.0: EmailLoginCode#verify (60) returns false for consumed/expired codes, burns one attempt atomically with UPDATE ... SET attempts = attempts + 1 WHERE attempts < MAX_ATTEMPTS (5) RETURNING attempts, then secure_compares code_hash with hash_code(submitted) and resets attempts to 0 on success; hash_code (45) is an HMAC-SHA256 keyed with GlobalSetting.safe_secret_key_base so a DB dump cannot enumerate the 6-digit space. The `active` scope also excludes attempts >= MAX_ATTEMPTS.

tasks.question: How does the built-in MCP server rotate OAuth refresh tokens, and what happens when an already-used refresh token is presented again (replay)?
tasks.search: mcp oauth refresh token rotation replay family revoke
tasks.verifiedBy: Read @v2026.9.0: TokenIssuer.refresh! (oauth.rb:301) locks the token row; if consumed_at is set it calls record.revoke_family! and raises InvalidAccess (replay); otherwise it checks revocation/expiry, client and resource, allows only narrowing scopes that keep the initial scope, validates the authorization and issues a new access token plus a new refresh token with the same family_id and parent: record. McpOauthRefreshToken.issue! (15) inherits the parent's expires_at and marks the parent consumed with replacement_id; revoke_family! (36) revokes every unrevoked token of the family.

tasks.question: When an upcoming change reaches the configured promotion status, how does Discourse decide whether to promote it automatically, and how does it make sure admins are notified only once?
tasks.search: upcoming change automatic promotion status notify admins once
tasks.verifiedBy: Read @v2026.9.0: UpcomingChanges::NotifyPromotion (notify_promotion.rb:24, Service::Base) chains policies setting_is_available, change_should_be_displayed, change_dependencies_met, meets_or_exceeds_status (-> UpcomingChanges.meets_or_exceeds_status?, lib/upcoming_changes.rb:164, compares status values with promote_upcoming_changes_on_status), promotion_not_already_handled (81, no automatically_promoted event yet), admin_has_not_manually_toggled (85) and should_notify_admins; then logs the promotion, notifies admins only if notify_admins? (109, no admins_notified_automatic_promotion event) and records the automatically_promoted event before triggering :upcoming_change_enabled. Called per setting by UpcomingChanges::NotifyPromotions from the CheckUpcomingChanges job.

tasks.question: How does an ActiveRecord model that declares `rate_limit` consume a rate-limiter slot when a record is created, and give the slot back when the record is destroyed or the transaction rolls back?
tasks.search: rate_limit model create record limiter rollback destroy
tasks.verifiedBy: Read @v2026.9.0: RateLimiter::OnCreateRecord::ClassMethods#rate_limit (on_create_record.rb:35) registers after_create (calls the limiter's performed! and remembers it in @performed), after_destroy (rollback!) and after_rollback (rollback! only if performed), all skipped when @rate_limits_disabled; default_rate_limiter (12) builds RateLimiter.new(user, "create_<model>", 1, rate_limit[_new_user]_create_<model> setting). RateLimiter#performed! (rate_limiter.rb:125) runs the PERFORM_LUA sliding-window script and raises LimitExceeded; rollback! (138) LPOPs the newest entry.
